requirement.original_user_excerpt: 2. The current frontend style needs adjustment. The current card contents are too small and not intuitive enough. When visiting on a PC, placing the mouse above the 3D model does not allow precise control of the 3D model. Extra introductions at the bottom of the card may appropriately be removed.
requirement.surface: Existing public PackJoyU product listing with inline 3D previews and inquiry links. This ruling does not change the project's named visual style, add checkout, or turn the site into a new application.

documented_rules.text: Enlarge the product preview area, remove repeated introductions at the bottom, and retain the name, essential specifications, category links, and inquiry button. Neither the geometric card nor the model preview area uses hover scale. When the mouse enters the model, pause automatic rotation and show a short operating hint; pressing inside the model viewport immediately gives that model pointer capture, and dragging over other cards still operates only the starting model. Card links and inquiry buttons are independent hit areas; ending a drag does not trigger a click.

Ordinary mouse wheels and trackpads always scroll the page. Only Ctrl/Cmd + wheel when the model control region is focused, or visible Zoom in / Zoom out buttons, zoom the camera; interception applies only to that model's modified-key zoom gesture, and other regions retain browser behavior. Escape, window blur, pointercancel, unmount, and navigation all release capture and listeners. This input rule applies to every product viewport in the shared Canvas; moving the mouse over another card cannot change activeSlug.

The model control region provides named left/right/up/down rotation controls, Zoom in, Zoom out, Reset view, Pause rotation, and Finish controls. After keyboard focus reaches the control region, arrow keys adjust orientation, and buttons provide the same function; Tab leaves normally, and Escape ends operation and returns to the source control. On touchscreens, only the model operating region takes over single-finger dragging; pinch zoom is constrained by camera bounds, and the text and button regions do not have whole-card touch-action:none. All touch targets are at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels. Explicit user pause and reduced-motion preferences are not overwritten when visible again (E-99 through E-102).

At PC widths of at least 1024px, product cards have a minimum width of 560px and the grid uses the auto-fit rule above; the model's visible viewport height is clamp(360px,28vw,440px), verified by actual container measurements at 1440px and 1920px, not only by increasing font size. Below 1024px, use one column or naturally wrap according to the 560px rule; the model viewport is 4:3 with a minimum height of 240px. When narrower than the target, width follows the container without horizontal scrolling. Frame the complete model/image boundaries; after reset do not crop the top, bottom, or outside packaging edges. The model toolbar is in an independent white-background region below the viewport and does not cover the subject.

Pointer-down inside the viewport directly captures the starting model; dragging across cards still operates only that model, without requiring an additional activation click. Hover pauses automatic rotation, and explicit user pause is not overwritten by becoming visible again. Ordinary wheel always scrolls the page; only Ctrl/Cmd + wheel when the model is focused, or explicit zoom buttons, changes the camera, constrained by product bounds. Escape, blur, pointercancel, route changes, and unmount release capture/listeners and restore normal scrolling. The hint is 'Drag to rotate · Ctrl/Cmd + wheel to zoom'; 'click to start' is not a mandatory mouse step.

Trigger: the pointer passes over a model and uses an ordinary mouse wheel or trackpad. Expected: the page still scrolls normally; only a focused model's Ctrl/Cmd + wheel or explicit zoom button changes the model camera; after exit all wheel interception is released.

Trigger: after keyboard focus reaches the model control region, use direction/zoom/reset controls. Expected: all controls have identifiable names, visible focus, and equivalent functions; Escape leaves operation and returns to the source control, without trapping Tab or automatically jumping to the product link.

Trigger: fingers drag/pinch inside the model viewport or swipe in the card's text region. Expected: verify model single-finger dragging, pinch zoom, and text-region page scrolling separately: only the model operating region takes over dragging, zoom cannot exceed the product's defined min/max, and text/page scrolling stays usable; measure every control's target at least 44 CSS px; no gesture submits an inquiry.

task.title: Fix direct model dragging and wheel focus
task.acceptance: 1) Direct pointer-down in the product card model viewport captures the current model; hover stops automatic rotation without geometric scaling. Ordinary wheel scrolls the page; only a focused model's Ctrl/Cmd + wheel or zoom controls zoom; do not force prior activation (E-97, E-98, E-99). 2) pointercancel, blur, Escape, and unmount all release input; subsequent operation targets the correct model without residual page-locking. User pause takes precedence over hide/show restoration. Keep tests that fail before the actual modification and pass afterward (E-100).

question: For the existing desktop Ctrl/Cmd+wheel interaction, which of the two explicit pointer-hit admission scopes should be proposed to clarify the ambiguous model-control-region wording: the same focused model's viewport plus its named toolbar, or that model's viewport only? Preserve every settled scrolling, focus, cross-model, touch, keyboard, camera-bound and release rule. Select among these two real options; do not infer new permissions or treat current code as the specification.

facts_not_preferences: ProductGallery.tsx lines 133-149 attaches its modified-wheel listener to the enclosing article while focusedSlug exists; it prevents default and changes that model's camera without separately filtering viewport, toolbar, or card body hit targets. This is a code-reading fact, not a browser reproduction or a reason to approve whole-card interception.

ProductGallery.tsx lines 211-260 has a focus wrapper containing both the model viewport and its named toolbar; internal focus transitions keep focusedSlug. Product names/specifications/category/inquiry links belong to the following body outside that wrapper. A .hint span is inside the viewport.

Independent white toolbar placement is a layout rule; touch-action rules concern touch input. Neither fact alone proves whether desktop modified-wheel over toolbar buttons must be admitted or excluded.

An operation-hint overlay and content-bearing title/description overlay are not automatically the same semantic region. Their actual hit classification remains a separate named risk; this choice cannot approve every viewport descendant by DOM containment alone.

common_definition_proposed_for_both_opti.focus_owner_i: The current actual DOM focus is in model i's viewport or in one of model i's named toolbar controls. Merely hovering, stale focusedSlug, or focus on the product's title/category/inquiry link does not count. Moving focus to another model or a non-control page element removes i's focus ownership. This definition is a proposed clarification to be documented, not a statement that every detail is already specified.
common_definition_proposed_for_both_opti.pointer_scope_difference: The alternatives differ only in whether modified-wheel hits on i's named toolbar/its buttons are admitted. Both admit a hit on i's actual model viewport when focus belongs to i. Both exclude non-control title/specification/category/inquiry regions and cross-model hits.
common_definition_proposed_for_both_opti.native: Do not preventDefault for the application and do not change any model camera; retain target-browser behavior. Ordinary wheel scrolls; Ctrl/Cmd+wheel commonly performs browser page zoom. Do not use a pure function result named scroll-page as proof of actual browser zoom.
common_definition_proposed_for_both_opti.unchanged: Direct model dragging does not require an extra activation click; explicit named Zoom button clicks remain functional; camera min/max limits remain; ordinary trackpad/wheel always scrolls the page; hover never steals focus; Escape/window blur/pointercancel/navigation/unmount release interception; established touch and keyboard behavior remains. No data migration, paid commitment, new dependency, whole-card touch capture, or extra downstream feature is introduced.

current.authority_limit: The requested deliverable is a planning-only ruling and a documentation-patch proposal. No code, canonical clause, task status, gate, API, or production behavior is changed by this call. A design pick does not waive review, real red-before/green-after evidence, or any settled requirement. If applying an option would change agreed scope rather than clarify this ambiguity, it must remain pending for owner authorization. Do not redesign the site's visual register or style.

options.A: Viewport plus the same model's named toolbar. Keep the shared proposed focus-owner definition: actual DOM focus in model i's viewport or named toolbar counts as focus belonging to i; hover and product-body focus do not. Admit Ctrl/Cmd+wheel only when that focus belongs to i and the pointer hits i's actual viewport or i's named toolbar/buttons. Change only i's camera within its existing bounds and prevent default only for that admitted event. The toolbar supports the same modified-wheel shortcut as the viewport, offering one continuous model-control surface; the tradeoff is that eligible modified-wheel over this toolbar does not perform browser page zoom. All ordinary wheel scrolling, non-control text/link native behavior, cross-model isolation, named button clicks, established keyboard/touch behavior and release conditions remain unchanged. Use semantic hit boundaries rather than the complete article. This is a small reversible event-routing and test clarification, with no new dependencies, data changes or external commitments.
options.B: Viewport only. Keep exactly the same shared proposed focus-owner definition: actual DOM focus in model i's viewport or named toolbar counts as focus belonging to i; hover and product-body focus do not. Admit Ctrl/Cmd+wheel only when that focus belongs to i and the pointer hits i's actual viewport. Change only i's camera within its existing bounds and prevent default only for that admitted event. The named toolbar/buttons always keep native browser behavior for modified-wheel, even when their model is focused; explicit Zoom button clicks still change the model camera. The camera wheel gesture is confined to the model image; the tradeoff is that a user with toolbar-button focus must move the pointer back over the viewport to use the modified-wheel camera shortcut. All ordinary wheel scrolling, non-control text/link native behavior, cross-model isolation, established keyboard/touch behavior and release conditions remain unchanged. Use semantic hit boundaries rather than the complete article. This is a small reversible event-routing and test clarification, with no new dependencies, data changes or external commitments.
